fieldMarks: Brown coat with darker head, neck and legs; old bulls can be pale yellowish.
Distinctive buff to yellowish-orange rump patch.
Bulls have widely branching antlers, typically six points per side, and a dark shaggy mane on the neck; antlers are shed annually.
Bulls average far heavier than cows (Montana: bulls over 1,000 lb, cows 500–600 lb).
behavior: Strongly gregarious; old cows lead summer herds of cows, calves and yearling spike bulls.
Rut in late September–early October; bulls bugle, gather harems and spar.
Feeds early morning and late evening; grazes grasses, sedges and forbs in summer and browses woody growth in winter.
Migrates by elevation in many areas: high in summer, low in winter.
habitat: Coniferous forest interspersed with openings (mountain meadows, grasslands, burns, logged areas); summers high and winters on grass and shrub ranges near thermal cover.
range: Western North America from Canada through the Rocky Mountains to New Mexico. Eastern populations were nearly eliminated and have been restored by transplants (e.g., to Michigan); introduced populations exist in Alaska.

lookalikes.name: Moose
lookalikes.howToTell: Elk are smaller than moose and larger than deer and caribou; in Scandinavia 'elk' refers to moose.
